## Trial `zram-swap-centos-stream10__MnMf3TW`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task are satisfied: node1 now has 1GB of zstd-compressed zram swap (exceeding the 512MB minimum), configured with swap-priority=100 and WantedBy=swap.target so it is preferred over any (currently absent) disk-backed swap, and its boot-time persistence was directly verified through an actual systemctl reboot with a confirmed boot_id change and automatic post-reboot restoration of the swap device. The executor also correctly diagnosed and fixed a mid-task misconfiguration (stale default zram device) via a bounded, fully-reverted corrective sequence rather than leaving broken state. Hygiene is high, with only a trivial leftover log file as residue.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.920 | 14/2 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap configured on node1
  - **Why:** Baseline showed zero swap and no zram-generator installed (cmd-0ebd427ae27f4a2e). Package installed (cmd-a7f187c1c15c413a) and /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf written specifying zram-size=1024, compression-algorithm=zstd (cmd-98811af2002b4ccc). After correcting a stale default-config device, zramctl/swapon directly show /dev/zram0 as a 1G zstd-compressed swap device active (cmd-462b4603b5384817, cmd-7cc98f5902a84955), well above the 512MB minimum.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0ebd427ae27f4a2e`, `cmd-a7f187c1c15c413a`, `cmd-98811af2002b4ccc`, `cmd-462b4603b5384817`, `cmd-7cc98f5902a84955`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Swap is active at boot (persists across restart)
  - **Why:** Pre-reboot healthy state captured (boot_id d052eb57, zram swap 1G zstd priority 100 active). A real reboot was triggered and acknowledged (cmd-92575ed3ab6743bd), connection loss observed during the transition (cmd-b8593ae57aee4bff, cmd-6f76ecb665604ad1), and a new boot_id (95c8ae0a) confirmed post-restart (cmd-0211663b1f5e4680), independently corroborated by the fixed before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. Post-reboot verification (cmd-ff43b9ce7c914da3) shows the 1G zstd zram swap automatically active again with priority 100, demonstrating the full disruption-and-recovery cycle required for a boot-persistence claim.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ae5d1fdbd6924d2f`, `cmd-92575ed3ab6743bd`, `cmd-b8593ae57aee4bff`, `cmd-6f76ecb665604ad1`, `cmd-0211663b1f5e4680`, `cmd-ff43b9ce7c914da3`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Zram swap is preferred over any disk-backed swap
  - **Why:** /etc/fstab contains no disk-backed swap entries (cmd-17a9a81fc59c421d), so there is no competing disk swap on node1. The zram swap unit dev-zram0.swap carries priority=100 (well above systemd's default disk-swap priority of -2) and is WantedBy=swap.target for automatic activation, so should a disk swap ever be added it would be de-prioritized. Given no disk swap exists to observe a live priority contest, this is satisfied on the basis of correct, verified configuration rather than an in-situ competition test.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-17a9a81fc59c421d`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. Command timeline reviewed chronologically. cmd-b7122ea3b4974796 (start /dev/zram0 + systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service) produced an unintended stale zram0 device using package-default settings (lzo-rle, ~1.7G) instead of the custom zstd/1024MB config (observed in cmd-cd50d083da674f81), because the module/generator picked up the default config file at /usr/lib/systemd/zram-generator.conf before the custom one took effect. This was fully diagnosed (cmd-aa07cdd9ca8e45a1, cmd-a12e86d1fdd5477a, read-only) and corrected via a bounded, fully-reverted sequence: swapoff, service stop, /sys/block/zram0/reset, and daemon-reload (cmd-e01c95668d5542fc), after which the setup was re-run and produced the correct 1G zstd device (cmd-462b4603b5384817, cmd-7cc98f5902a84955). This qualifies as a corrective action to fix an earlier attempt rather than an unnecessary mutation, and left no incorrect residue. The reboot trigger (cmd-92575ed3ab6743bd) is a necessary, low-risk action to collect bounded final evidence for the boot-persistence requirement and the provider-wide restart protocol. Minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log was left behind from the reboot trigger redirect, a trivial, non-security-relevant log file (visible in after_executor temporary-files diff). No failed services, no unsafe exposure changes, and package health remained consistent (manager=dnf) before and after.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-b7122ea3b4974796`, `cmd-cd50d083da674f81`, `cmd-aa07cdd9ca8e45a1`, `cmd-a12e86d1fdd5477a`, `cmd-e01c95668d5542fc`, `cmd-462b4603b5384817`, `cmd-7cc98f5902a84955`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`
